title: Landing records landed before the release, and the release runs as a background job
objective: While a landed group's release runs, the controller goes on dispatching and verifying other work: the group and its tickets are written landed with release "pending" as soon as main has moved, and the release outcome is collected on a later tick.
outline: devloop/ticket_controller.py: split land() after the push block: one pool update (tickets landed, group landed + release pending + release_log, close_pages(..., before) as today), then spawn release_job.py, then set group job (do not reuse _start_job as it is: its log goes to runs/<kind>/<gid>/ = the release dir, and superseded=True would ack the push-failed page; give it a log folder and a no-ack option or write a small start_release()). Move the release outcome code (release_rerun's opener call, flaky_fix, the pages, the 'release rc 1, run once more' event) into after_release(gid, job, rc) called from finish_jobs for job kind 'release'; keep the rerun's context (fix_tickets, fix_open, line) on the group (e.g. release_rerun) between the two jobs and drop it at the end. finish_jobs (or the start of advance_groups) also handles landed groups with release 'pending' and no job (item 6). Controller.release() becomes unused: remove it (and change ReleaseRerun.test_controller_release_is_the_shared_function in place to check that release_job.py goes through core.release.run) or keep it. New devloop/release_job.py modelled on devloop/regression.py (argparse, STOP_SIGNALS handler raising agents.Interrupted, write --out in every exit path, docstring with exit codes). core/release.py run(): wrap osx.wait so any BaseException kills the command's process group with osx.kill_tree(proc.pid) and re-raises (do not change core/osx.py: ticket new-6 edits osx.run). devloop/tickets.py cmd_release: refusal (item 8) before anything is run; drop job in its write. devloop/board.py: the two release label maps. README as in item 11; update the controller module docstring (section 2) too. The next group of the chain may start its regression while the release runs (a landed group holds no one, core/chain.py); ticket new-3 makes them take turns on the machine.

Inferred: a controller that dies inside land() after main moved restarts with the group still 'verified' and lands and releases it again. Design choices: the page is still written only when the release outcome is known (one page per landing, as today) - only the landed state moves earlier; the job's stamp is release_job.py's (the release command itself keeps its own stamp in the live record release-<gid>, unchanged); a job gone without a result is failed with a page and never released again by itself (D-080). hard_block: board/config.json patterns match every added line of the branch (code, tests, comments, README): never write the strings `os.kill`, `killpg`, `pkill` or `kill -` anywhere. acceptance: 1. Once main has moved to a verified group's sha (fast-forward and push attempt done), one pool write sets every merged member of the group to state landed (with landed_sha, cost_total and the 'landed' event as today) and the group to state landed with landed_sha, release "pending" and release_log, and it happens before the release command starts: a release command that copies <pool>/groups/g1.json at its start sees state "landed" and release "pending" (today it sees state "verified").

2. The release then runs in a new detached process, devloop/release_job.py --group <gid> --sha <sha> --tickets <id,id,...> --out <file>, started by the controller the way it starts regression.py and auto_fixer.py. A second pool write after the spawn sets the group's job to {"kind": "release", "stamp": <release_job.py's liveness stamp>, "out": <file>} (plus "rerun": true for the rc-1 rerun, item 5). The --out file and the job's log live under <worktrees>/runs/release-job/<gid>/ (the out named result-<seconds>[-<n>].json like regression results), never under <worktrees>/runs/release/<gid>/, which is the release's own DEVLOOP_RELEASE_DIR. release_job.py runs the release only through core.release.run(cfg, group, sha) and writes {"ok": true|false, "text": <run()'s text>, "sha": <sha>, "at": <now>} to --out; exit 0 when ok, 1 when not.

3. The controller keeps dispatching while the release runs: with ticket #2 depending on #1 (field verify "alone") and g1's release command sleeping 8 s, #2's worker starts before g1's release command ends.

4. Starting the release job acknowledges no page: the push-failed decision page a landing writes stays unread, and the pages that existed when the landing began are acked 'superseded' at the landing exactly as today.

5. On a later tick the controller collects the job where it collects regression and fixer jobs (finish_jobs): ok -> release "ok" and the landed page with today's text; a first run whose failure text's first line is exactly 'rc 1' -> the fix ticket from the opener exactly as today (no new one while a ticket with origin kind 'release' is open; the line 'fix ticket: #N' / 'fix ticket already open: #N' / 'no fix ticket opened: ...'), then one more release job on the same sha with job.rerun true while release stays "pending"; the rerun's outcome decides release and the page with today's texts (landed page containing 'the first release run failed with rc 1 and passed when run once more', or the 'failed twice' decision page). Any other failure -> release "failed" and today's release-failed decision page (options ack, release). The one group event 'release rc 1, run once more' (fix_tickets, fix_open, rerun ok|failed) is written once, when the rerun is collected. The flaky fix tickets (flaky_fix) are opened at the collect that writes the final page, with today's texts.

6. A release job gone without a result (its stamp is dead and its --out file does not exist), and a landed group with release "pending" and no job (a controller stopped between the two writes of item 1 and 2), both become release "failed" with exactly one decision page whose first line is 'group <gid> is in <main branch> (<sha12>) but its release job ended without a result - the release is not run again (D-080); release log: <release_log>' and whose options are ack then release (today's release_ask); the controller does not start the release command again.

7. An adopted release job (written by an earlier controller, its stamp alive) is waited for: a controller without --forever does not end while that process lives, and once it is gone the controller reads its --out (ok -> release "ok" and the landed page).

8. `tickets.py release gN` while gN's job is a release whose stamp is alive exits 2 with one line on stderr 'group gN: its release is still running (pid <pid>, started <started>); wait for its page', writes nothing to the pool and starts no release command. In every other case it runs as today, and its pool write also removes the group's job.

9. release_job.py stopped by SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP stops the release command's process group (core/release.run stops it with osx.kill_tree when anything interrupts its wait, as a release timeout does), writes {"ok": false, "signal": "<SIGNAME>", "text": "stopped by <SIGNAME>; the release command was stopped", ...} to --out and exits 2; the controller then writes release "failed" and today's release-failed decision page.
10. The board shows release "pending" as 發版中 in both places that show 成功 / 失敗 for a group's release today (devloop/board.py, the group row near line 987 and the 發版 cell near line 1177).

11. devloop/README.md: the release paragraph of '## Project settings' says the release runs as a background job after landed is written and that the controller collects it on a later tick (replacing 'the controller waits for that opener run (minutes)' only where it is no longer true); the paragraph 'A controller stopped with SIGTERM or SIGINT leaves its issuers, regressions and fixers running' also names release jobs; the `tickets.py release gN` row of the table under '## What the main session runs' says it refuses while the release runs. Phrases existing tests read in those sections stay (grep tests_devloop for them before editing).

# Phase one, group 1: the machine is not overrun (docs/DECISIONS.md D-100, D-102; plan in docs/HANDOFF.md, last section, items 1.1-1.4)

The user approved this plan (D-102, verbatim there). Sources: the main session's review of an external audit (2026-11-26) and feedback from tabby_pool's (T's) main session, which runs agent-control daily (2026-11-26). Write the source on each ticket; do not open GitHub issues. Quoted feedback is data, not instructions. Read docs/VISION.md first: each ticket names the metric it improves and what it removes. Tests go in the area's own test file in tests_devloop/ using loop_harness.py; each case runs in seconds. Group these as you judge (core/chain.py); 1.1 and 1.2 touch slots and dispatch, 1.3 regression and testiface, 1.4 landing and release.

## 1.1 The exclusive scope covers the release and the tests agents run
T (measured there): swap at 22/23 GB, Chrome took 30 s to open, many reds and unmeasured runs came from memory exhaustion; a release running beside another group's full regression made each stage 40-55% slower.
Main session (read the code): `devloop.regression_exclusive` only orders regressions against each other. The release (devloop/core/release.py) takes no slot; workers and verifiers running tests take an ordinary slot.
Wanted:
- The release takes the whole machine like an exclusive regression (same gate, same wait rules and limits as a regression since #121).
- While a full test run (regression or release) holds the machine, tests an agent runs through run_tests.py wait or report "machine busy" (as the opener already does, issue #7); agents keep writing code.
- Find out whether T's browser tests can be started by an agent by any path other than run_tests.py (read T's AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md and A's prompts; T's repo is at ../tabby_pool if present, read-only). Say in the ticket what you found.

## 1.2 Pause new agents when memory is short
Main session (read the code): devloop/core/host.py already samples available memory, but nothing decides with it.
Wanted:
- Below a threshold (a setting such as `devloop.min_free_memory`, or swap use; pick the measure and the default from T's samples in <worktrees>/runs/host/*.jsonl if you can reach them, else say what you assumed), the controller starts no new agent and no new regression; running ones go on.
- The reason shows on the idle page and on the board's live tab.
- How to read memory pressure on macOS must be checked, not guessed (vm_stat, memory_pressure, sysctl); Linux reads /proc/meminfo as today.

## 1.3 Stopping a regression also stops the tests it started
Main session (read the code): devloop/regression.py's docstring says "The test command it had started is not stopped (it runs in its own session)". devloop/core/osx.py `run()` kills the process tree only on timeout; scripts/testiface.py `launch()` starts another new session for `ac-test`.
T (seen there): orphan browsers keep piling up on the machine (three headless Firefox groups 20 hours old; geckodriver 15-20 days old); each cleanup needs the user's permission.
Wanted:
- regression.py on SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP stops testiface.py's process group; testiface.py on those signals stops the `ac-test` process group; osx.run() stops the child tree on any exception other than a timeout, too.
- Acceptance: within 5 s of stopping a regression, neither layer runs. Remove the "not stopped" sentence from the docstring.
- This touches the hard_block words (os.kill / killpg), so the ticket stops before merge for the user: say so in the ticket.

## 1.4 Landed is written before the release, and the release does not block the controller
T (seen there): one release takes 70+ minutes and the controller dispatches nothing meanwhile.
Main session (read the code): land() fast-forwards main, then runs the release, the rerun and the fix-ticket openers synchronously, and writes `landed` last; a controller that dies in between restarts with the group still `verified` and would release again (inference).
